text:
Carmen (sales): Quick ask from client HelixCare: prepping a Private deploy POC. They want guidance: VPC peering vs interface endpoint (PrivateLink), how to whitelist a single egress IP for their firewall, exact minimal ports to open, and whether SNI and original client IP survive. ETA: they want answers before the sales call tomorrow morning.

Leo (netops): TL;DR: Peering preserves source IP (so audits/netflow show original). PrivateLink uses ENIs in the customer's VPC and the connector appears to come from that ENI IP -> not original client IP.

Sofia (eng): For HTTP we can surface original client IP in headers over PrivateLink (X-Original-Client-IP / X-Forwarded-For). For raw TLS streams (gRPC/streaming over TLS) the TCP source will be the ENI; app-level header is only for HTTP.

Dmitri (security): If their compliance requires network-level source IP for forensics, recommend peering or an in-VPC proxy that forwards original IP via a signed header. If they accept app-level audit, PrivateLink + header is fine.

Leo (netops): Minimal port list (customer-facing VPC rules):
- Outbound: 443 TCP to our control plane (we'll provide CIDR during handshake)
- Inbound (if using PrivateLink): 443 TCP from connector ENI range (provided at setup)
- If peering: allow 443 TCP over peering route table.

Sofia (eng): Example SG snippet (replace with customer CIDRs):
```
# customer security group rules - minimal
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to 52.11.0.0/16   # example control plane
- If PrivateLink: Allow inbound TCP 443 from <connector-eni-cidr>
- Allow outbound to NTP (123/udp) if system clocks required
```

Carmen (sales): They also asked for a single static egress IP (their appliance only allows one IP). Can we guarantee one IP?

Leo (netops): Yes: have them route connector egress through a NAT Gateway with an Elastic IP in their account. With peering the source IP is preserved so if they want a fixed egress on our side they'd need to NAT on their edge. With PrivateLink the ENI is internal; outbound egress can be NATed to a single EIP we don't control.

Sofia (eng): Operational notes:
- If they expect >500Mbps sustained, recommend peering + TGW + dedicated subnet for connector to avoid asymmetric routing and MTU fragmentation.
- For burst RPS SLAs we can offer a Dedicated capacity commit (commercial) rather than best-effort Private deploy.

Dmitri (security): SNI: TLS ClientHello SNI is visible unless the client implements ESNI; middleboxes may rewrite SNI. If they perform TLS interception, they must preserve headers/identity; otherwise we recommend end-to-end TLS to our connector.

infra-bot: Handshake ticket created: https://redwood.internal/handshakes/HC-2026-42  — netops to upload connector ENI ranges and final SG examples.

Carmen (sales): Can someone draft 2 bullet answers I can paste into the RFP: one about logs/data retention, one about key management? Need short copy.

Dmitri (security): Paste-ready: "Data: request metadata and operational logs are retained per customer-configured retention in the Private deploy control plane; payload contents are not stored unless explicitly enabled by the customer. Keys: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; we integrate with cloud KMS or external HSM via PKCS#11."

Leo (netops): I'll attach the ENI CIDR ranges and a sample SG + NAT pattern to the handshake ticket by COB. Planning note: if they pick PrivateLink and insist on file/port-level IDS signatures, they should plan to re-inject X-Forwarded-For into app logs.

Sofia (eng): I'll add MTU/buffer tuning notes and a recommendation for token batching to reduce egress bytes for the POC.

Carmen (sales): Perfect — I'll send to HelixCare and confirm peering vs PrivateLink choice on tomorrow's call. Thanks all. :rocket:
